rounds.text: SJP Ultrasonics Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an accessible P/E of 20.6x [E1] while sitting only 35% of the way up its 52-week range [E4]. The business demonstrates elite profitability and compounding power, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 32% [E13], a 3-year compounded profit growth of 56% [E15], and a stellar 3-year median ROE of 38% [E18]. Furthermore, operating margins have expanded by 8 percentage points to 31% [E20], supported by structural operational improvements like debtor days dropping from 125 to 91.7 days [E39]. Institutional confidence is surging with positive money flow and a 3.80 percentage point increase in institutional holdings [E32], while the underlying Capital Goods sector enjoys a strong macro tailwind score of +0.59 [E46]. Valuation models indicate substantial upside, with a discounted cash flow yielding a 46.0% margin of safety [E34] and a reverse DCF showing the current price only prices in a modest 9.4% earnings growth compared to the 18.0% base case assumption [E35]. Conceded: operating cash flow is negative at Rs -3.51 Cr resulting in a cash conversion ratio of -0.67x for Mar 2026 [E23, E24].

Significant cracks beneath the surface of SJP Ultrasonics Ltd are exposed by severe cash flow deterioration, as operating cash flow plunges to negative Rs 3.51 Cr and free cash flow drops to negative Rs 3.91 Cr in Mar 2026, driving cash conversion down to an alarming -0.67x [E23, E24, E25]. This cash burn forces the company to increase its borrowings to Rs 6.52 Cr as of Sep 2026, moving up from Rs 5.78 Cr a year prior [E27]. Furthermore, insiders are bailing out aggressively, with promoter holding crashing by 21.51 percentage points in a single month down to 58.00% in Oct 2026 from 79.51% in Sep 2026 [E29]. Operational stability is also questionable given that both the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are explicitly flagged as inconsistent [E21, E22]. Finally, shareholders receive zero reward for holding these risks, as the dividend yield sits completely flat at 0.00% [E3]. Conceded: [E33].

While the bear highlights negative cash flow [E23, E24, E25], this must be weighed against the company’s structural efficiency, evidenced by a superior ROA of 19.83% compared to the 6.19% sector benchmark [E7] and a robust 3-year median ROE of 38% [E18]. The increase in borrowings [E27] remains manageable given the company's moderate leverage of 0.31x [E26] and its ability to deliver consistent multi-year sales and profit growth [E43, E44]. Regarding the promoter stake reduction [E29], this transition has been met with immediate confidence from institutional investors, as evidenced by the positive money flow and the entry of both foreign and domestic institutions into the stock [E30, E31, E32]. While operating margins are flagged as inconsistent [E21, E22], the company has successfully expanded its operating margin to 31% from 24% over the last three years [E20]. Conceded: the lack of dividends [E3] and the negative cash conversion [E23]. Ultimately, the market is mispricing the company’s growth potential, as the current price implies only 9.4% earnings growth against the 18% base case assumption [E35].

The bull attempts to downplay negative cash flows [E23, E24, E25] by pointing to structural efficiency metrics like ROA [E7] and ROE [E18], but high accounting returns mean little when operating cash flow is outright negative at Rs -3.51 Cr [E24] and free cash flow is an alarming Rs -3.91 Cr [E25]. Conceded: the company delivers consistent multi-year sales and profit growth [E43, E44], but this growth is aggressively capital-consuming rather than cash-generative, resulting in a cash conversion ratio of -0.67x [E23]. While the bull dismisses rising borrowings [E27] using moderate leverage figures [E26], total borrowings have actually expanded to Rs 6.52 Cr from Rs 5.78 Cr [E27] precisely while cash burn accelerates. Furthermore, the bull characterizes promoter stake reduction [E29] as a mere handover to institutions [E30, E31, E32], glossing over the massive insider exodus of 21.51 percentage points in a single month [E29]. Finally, relying on implied growth rates from reverse DCF models [E35] ignores the structural reality of inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating margins [E21, E22] that directly undermine predictable future earnings.
